title: CAP theorem in practice

curriculum.learner_outcome: Distinguish availability from consistency guarantees during an actual network partition.
curriculum.production_scenario: A two-region inventory service loses its replication link during checkout.
misconceptions: CAP does not mean permanently choosing any two features independently of failures.
curriculum.evidence: Trace accepted and rejected operations on both sides of the partition.
curriculum.artifact: A partition timeline with explicit inventory correctness and availability decisions.

title: Consistency models: linearizability to eventual

curriculum.learner_outcome: Compare observed read histories and select a consistency guarantee for each operation.
curriculum.production_scenario: Profile edits appear old after a user switches to another region.
misconceptions: A replicated database does not automatically provide read-your-writes across every client route.
curriculum.evidence: Classify three read histories and identify the violated guarantee.
curriculum.artifact: An annotated request history and a client routing consistency policy.

title: Load balancing strategies (L4 vs L7)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose connection or request routing from workload and health-check evidence.
curriculum.production_scenario: Long-lived streaming clients leave one backend overloaded while peers remain idle.
misconceptions: Round robin does not imply equal work when requests have different costs.
curriculum.evidence: Replay mixed request durations and compare maximum backend queue depth.
curriculum.artifact: A load distribution table with a justified health-check configuration.

title: Horizontal vs vertical scaling trade-offs

curriculum.learner_outcome: Locate the bottleneck before choosing a larger machine or additional replicas.
curriculum.production_scenario: An image API adds replicas but the shared database still saturates.
misconceptions: Adding machines does not remove a shared serial bottleneck.
curriculum.evidence: Estimate throughput bounds before and after two proposed capacity changes.
curriculum.artifact: A resource budget and a scaling decision with measurable stop conditions.

title: Latency numbers and back-of-envelope estimation

curriculum.learner_outcome: Estimate end-to-end latency and capacity using explicit measurements and assumptions.
curriculum.production_scenario: A checkout endpoint must meet a latency objective during a traffic burst.
misconceptions: Adding average component times does not predict the tail of parallel requests.
curriculum.evidence: Calculate optimistic and pessimistic budgets and validate one assumption experimentally.
curriculum.artifact: A latency worksheet identifying dominant costs and uncertain measurements.

title: Stateless vs stateful service design

curriculum.learner_outcome: Place durable and session state deliberately so request routing survives process loss.
curriculum.production_scenario: A deployment drains a server holding every active shopping cart.
misconceptions: A stateless API still depends on state somewhere in the system.
curriculum.evidence: Kill a simulated worker and explain which user state survives.
curriculum.artifact: A state ownership diagram and a restart recovery demonstration.

title: Idempotency and exactly-once semantics

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design retried operations that preserve one intended business effect under duplication.
curriculum.production_scenario: A checkout client retries after payment succeeded but its response timed out.
misconceptions: A retry token alone is insufficient without atomic association to the effect.
curriculum.evidence: Replay duplicate requests including the same token with different payloads.
curriculum.artifact: An idempotency record schema and a duplicate-request test transcript.

title: Time, clocks, and ordering in distributed systems

curriculum.learner_outcome: Separate wall-clock display from ordering and elapsed-time measurements across machines.
curriculum.production_scenario: Two workers disagree about whether a lease expired during a clock correction.
misconceptions: Increasing timestamps from different hosts do not prove causal ordering.
curriculum.evidence: Construct an offset timeline that breaks a wall-clock ordering assumption.
curriculum.artifact: A clock-failure trace and explicit timestamp semantics for service events.

title: Consensus: Raft and leader election

curriculum.learner_outcome: Explain how a replicated log remains safe across leader replacement and partitions.
curriculum.production_scenario: A metadata leader crashes after accepting a write but before replying.
misconceptions: A new leader cannot safely commit arbitrary local entries without quorum rules.
curriculum.evidence: Trace terms and commit indexes through one failed leader transition.
curriculum.artifact: A three-node log timeline showing committed and discarded entries.

title: Quorum reads/writes and tunable consistency

curriculum.learner_outcome: Evaluate quorum overlap alongside versioning, failure handling and consistency guarantees.
curriculum.production_scenario: A replicated cart store serves stale values despite overlapping replica counts.
misconceptions: R plus W greater than N alone does not establish linearizability in every implementation.
curriculum.evidence: Compare read results under stale versions and a changing replica set.
curriculum.artifact: A quorum experiment matrix with assumptions stated beside each claim.

title: Consistent hashing and virtual nodes

curriculum.learner_outcome: Measure key movement and load balance when a hash ring changes membership.
curriculum.production_scenario: A cache expansion causes a miss storm and uneven node memory usage.
misconceptions: Balanced key counts do not imply balanced traffic for hot keys.
curriculum.evidence: Compare moved keys and busiest-node traffic for modulo and ring assignment.
curriculum.artifact: A deterministic ring simulator with membership-change and skew reports.

title: Database sharding and partition strategies

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose a partition key by testing query locality, growth and skew.
curriculum.production_scenario: A tenant-based split concentrates one large customer's writes on one shard.
misconceptions: More shards do not split an indivisible hot key automatically.
curriculum.evidence: Run representative queries against two partition maps and count fan-out.
curriculum.artifact: A shard-key decision record and a migration sketch with rollback.

title: Replication: leader-follower, multi-leader, leaderless

curriculum.learner_outcome: Match durability and read behavior to replication mode and failover policy.
curriculum.production_scenario: A primary fails after acknowledging a write that a replica has not replayed.
misconceptions: Acknowledgment does not always mean every replica has persisted the write.
curriculum.evidence: Trace acknowledged writes through failure under two replication settings.
curriculum.artifact: A replication topology and a documented data-loss boundary.

title: LSM trees vs B-trees

curriculum.learner_outcome: Relate storage-engine design to measured read, write and space amplification.
curriculum.production_scenario: An ingestion service develops latency spikes while background compaction runs.
misconceptions: Write-optimized does not mean writes have no deferred maintenance cost.
curriculum.evidence: Compare ingestion and lookup costs as immutable run count grows.
curriculum.artifact: A storage-engine comparison worksheet with a compaction budget.

title: Database indexes: how they work and when they hurt

curriculum.learner_outcome: Select indexes by measuring query plans and the extra cost of writes.
curriculum.production_scenario: A reporting query stays slow after an index is added to the wrong leading column.
misconceptions: An index is not always cheaper than scanning most table rows.
curriculum.evidence: Compare query plans before and after an index and measure insert overhead.
curriculum.artifact: A reproducible SQL workload with explained index decisions.

title: SQL vs NoSQL: choosing a datastore

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose a datastore from required invariants, access patterns and operational constraints.
curriculum.production_scenario: An order service needs joins for reporting and strict inventory updates.
misconceptions: SQL and NoSQL labels do not determine every consistency or scaling property.
curriculum.evidence: Map each workload requirement to a concrete supported operation or limitation.
curriculum.artifact: A datastore decision matrix including rejected alternatives and migration risks.

title: Transactions and isolation levels

curriculum.learner_outcome: Reproduce concurrency anomalies and choose isolation or locking for an invariant.
curriculum.production_scenario: Two booking transactions each observe the final seat as available.
misconceptions: A transaction boundary alone does not prevent all concurrent anomalies.
curriculum.evidence: Interleave two SQL sessions and prove whether overbooking remains possible.
curriculum.artifact: A concurrency test transcript and a retry-aware reservation transaction.

title: Distributed transactions: 2PC and sagas

curriculum.learner_outcome: Compare atomic commit and compensation when one business operation spans services.
curriculum.production_scenario: An order reserves stock but payment fails after a network timeout.
misconceptions: A saga compensation is a business action rather than a universal rollback.
curriculum.evidence: Trace crash points and name the durable recovery action at each point.
curriculum.artifact: A transaction state table and a compensation contract for checkout.

title: Object storage internals (S3-style systems)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design object identity, metadata and upload recovery around documented storage guarantees.
curriculum.production_scenario: A media upload finishes after its metadata transaction times out.
misconceptions: Object storage is not a local filesystem with arbitrary rename semantics.
curriculum.evidence: Trace incomplete uploads and verify metadata never advertises missing content.
curriculum.artifact: An upload state machine with cleanup rules and version handling.

title: Time-series databases and downsampling

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design metric storage that controls cardinality and supports bounded time-range reads.
curriculum.production_scenario: A telemetry service runs out of memory after user IDs become metric labels.
misconceptions: A timestamp column alone does not solve metric retention or cardinality growth.
curriculum.evidence: Estimate series count and scan size before and after removing a label.
curriculum.artifact: A metric schema and retention budget with cardinality guardrails.

title: OLTP vs OLAP and the data warehouse

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose partitioning and clustering from analytical access patterns and freshness needs.
curriculum.production_scenario: Daily revenue reports scan years of data to answer one week's question.
misconceptions: Warehouse performance cannot be inferred from row count without bytes scanned.
curriculum.evidence: Compare query bytes and ingestion latency for two physical layouts.
curriculum.artifact: An analytical model and a partition-pruning experiment with cost assumptions.

title: Change data capture pipelines

curriculum.learner_outcome: Explain how change streams support downstream views without losing source ordering context.
curriculum.production_scenario: A search index misses updates while transitioning from its initial snapshot.
misconceptions: CDC does not automatically make downstream consumers exactly-once or schema-proof.
curriculum.evidence: Trace snapshot overlap, duplicate changes and a consumer restart.
curriculum.artifact: A change-stream checkpoint contract and a replay reconciliation procedure.

title: Caching strategies: write-through, aside, back

curriculum.learner_outcome: Select a cache policy by stating freshness, durability and origin-load requirements.
curriculum.production_scenario: A product detail API returns an outdated price after a successful edit.
misconceptions: Writing the database and cache separately does not make them atomic.
curriculum.evidence: Simulate read/update interleavings and identify stale or lost results.
curriculum.artifact: A cache policy table and a reproducible stale-read trace.

title: Cache invalidation and stampede protection

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design invalidation behavior that bounds staleness under races and missed notifications.
curriculum.production_scenario: A delayed cache fill reinstalls an old profile just after invalidation.
misconceptions: Deleting a key does not prevent an older in-flight read from writing it back.
curriculum.evidence: Replay the stale-fill race and compare TTL and versioned-key fixes.
curriculum.artifact: An invalidation timeline with an explicit acceptable staleness budget.

title: Redis internals and data structures

curriculum.learner_outcome: Connect Redis data structures, persistence and eviction to workload behavior.
curriculum.production_scenario: A session cache evicts active sessions when a new workload fills memory.
misconceptions: In-memory storage does not imply identical durability or latency under every configuration.
curriculum.evidence: Compare recovery expectations and eviction results for two configurations.
curriculum.artifact: A Redis workload configuration with memory and recovery acceptance checks.

title: CDNs and edge caching

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose edge caching rules that preserve identity, freshness and origin capacity.
curriculum.production_scenario: An edge cache accidentally shares a personalized response between users.
misconceptions: A CDN cannot safely cache every successful response under the URL alone.
curriculum.evidence: Derive cache keys for public and personalized routes and test revalidation.
curriculum.artifact: An edge caching contract with private-data exclusions and expiry rules.

title: Kafka internals: partitions, offsets, ISR

curriculum.learner_outcome: Trace durable partition logs, consumer offsets and replication through failure.
curriculum.production_scenario: A consumer processes a record then crashes before committing its offset.
misconceptions: Kafka ordering is per partition rather than one global order for a topic.
curriculum.evidence: Trace duplicate processing after restart and compare acknowledgment settings.
curriculum.artifact: A partition/consumer diagram with a recovery and offset test transcript.

title: Message queues vs pub/sub vs streams

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose queue acknowledgment and retry behavior from the cost of losing or duplicating work.
curriculum.production_scenario: An email worker crashes between sending a message and acknowledging it.
misconceptions: A queue does not make an external side effect exactly-once by itself.
curriculum.evidence: Simulate crashes before and after the side effect and inspect redelivery.
curriculum.artifact: A worker state machine and bounded retry/dead-letter handling rules.

title: Delivery guarantees: at-most, at-least, exactly-once

curriculum.learner_outcome: Separate message delivery claims from atomic processing of business effects.
curriculum.production_scenario: A redelivered event charges an account twice despite reliable transport.
misconceptions: Exactly-once transport is not a blanket guarantee for external payment effects.
curriculum.evidence: Replay a duplicate event at each crash point around the database commit.
curriculum.artifact: An effect ledger schema and an idempotent consumer test suite.

title: Event sourcing and CQRS

curriculum.learner_outcome: Model an append-only business history and rebuild views with compatible event versions.
curriculum.production_scenario: A balance projection must be rebuilt after correcting projection logic.
misconceptions: An event log is not automatically a good domain model or an audit policy.
curriculum.evidence: Replay old and new event versions and compare reconstructed balances.
curriculum.artifact: A versioned event contract and a projection rebuild transcript.

title: Transactional outbox and dual-write problem

curriculum.learner_outcome: Make local state changes and eventual publication recoverable across relay failures.
curriculum.production_scenario: An order commits but its event publication fails during a broker outage.
misconceptions: The outbox removes a dual-write gap but can still publish duplicates.
curriculum.evidence: Crash the relay around publication and verify no committed order is forgotten.
curriculum.artifact: An outbox schema with replay tests and a consumer deduplication rule.

title: Stream processing: windows, watermarks, state

curriculum.learner_outcome: Define event-time windows and correction behavior for delayed and repeated events.
curriculum.production_scenario: A regional outage delivers purchase events after their reporting window closed.
misconceptions: A watermark is a completeness estimate rather than proof no late event exists.
curriculum.evidence: Feed out-of-order events and explain emitted totals and later corrections.
curriculum.artifact: A windowing policy and an event trace with expected aggregate revisions.

title: Backpressure and load shedding

curriculum.learner_outcome: Bound queued work and propagate overload without growing memory indefinitely.
curriculum.production_scenario: A slow downstream writer causes the upstream API to accumulate requests.
misconceptions: Buffering more work delays failure when sustained arrival exceeds service capacity.
curriculum.evidence: Graph queue depth under sustained overload and compare two admission limits.
curriculum.artifact: A bounded worker prototype with queue, rejection and latency measurements.

title: Circuit breakers, retries, and timeouts

curriculum.learner_outcome: Protect callers from repeated dependency failures while allowing controlled recovery probes.
curriculum.production_scenario: A failing recommendation dependency consumes every checkout worker thread.
misconceptions: A circuit breaker does not replace timeouts or guarantee the dependency recovers.
curriculum.evidence: Inject failures and show the transition from rejection to bounded probing.
curriculum.artifact: A breaker state diagram with timeout and recovery test cases.

title: Rate limiting algorithms

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose a request admission algorithm that bounds burst and sustained load.
curriculum.production_scenario: A client sends bursts around minute boundaries and overwhelms a shared API.
misconceptions: Equal average rates do not imply equal permitted bursts.
curriculum.evidence: Replay boundary bursts and compare accepted requests under two algorithms.
curriculum.artifact: A deterministic limiter simulator and an endpoint failure-policy decision.

title: Graceful degradation and fallback design

curriculum.learner_outcome: Preserve essential user operations by shedding optional work under dependency failure.
curriculum.production_scenario: A recommendation outage should not prevent customers from paying for existing carts.
misconceptions: Returning partial data is only safe when clients understand its missing guarantees.
curriculum.evidence: Disable each optional dependency and verify checkout invariants still hold.
curriculum.artifact: A degradation matrix with user-visible behavior and recovery tests.

title: Chaos engineering and failure injection

curriculum.learner_outcome: Form a falsifiable resilience hypothesis and bound an experiment's impact.
curriculum.production_scenario: A team wants evidence that one unavailable replica does not break reads.
misconceptions: Randomly breaking production is not a substitute for a scoped hypothesis.
curriculum.evidence: Run a local fault scenario and compare measured behavior with the hypothesis.
curriculum.artifact: An experiment record with safeguards, observations and a follow-up fix.

title: Disaster recovery: RPO, RTO, multi-region

curriculum.learner_outcome: Derive backup and restore procedures from explicit recovery-time and data-loss objectives.
curriculum.production_scenario: A database operator must recover from accidental deletion that replication already copied.
misconceptions: Replication is not a backup against destructive logical changes.
curriculum.evidence: Restore a small dataset to a chosen point and verify application invariants.
curriculum.artifact: A timed recovery runbook with restored-data checks and measured gaps.

title: Hot partitions and celebrity problems

curriculum.learner_outcome: Identify workload skew and distinguish hot keys from poor partition distribution.
curriculum.production_scenario: A celebrity account dominates one otherwise evenly sized feed shard.
misconceptions: Hashing keys evenly does not distribute one key's requests across owners.
curriculum.evidence: Compare uniform and skewed traffic against the same partition map.
curriculum.artifact: A skew report and a split/cache plan with consistency implications.

title: Thundering herd and connection storms

curriculum.learner_outcome: Prevent synchronized expiry and retries from multiplying origin load.
curriculum.production_scenario: Many workers refill the same popular key immediately after cache expiry.
misconceptions: A larger cache alone does not prevent simultaneous misses on one key.
curriculum.evidence: Plot origin calls during expiry with and without coalesced refresh.
curriculum.artifact: A cache-refresh prototype with burst and failure traces.

title: API design: REST, gRPC, GraphQL trade-offs

curriculum.learner_outcome: Define resource operations with explicit errors, retry semantics and pagination behavior.
curriculum.production_scenario: Clients cannot tell whether a timed-out creation request succeeded.
misconceptions: An HTTP verb by itself does not establish a complete business contract.
curriculum.evidence: Exercise create, retry, validation failure and pagination while data changes.
curriculum.artifact: An API contract with request/response examples and invariant tests.

title: API versioning and backward compatibility

curriculum.learner_outcome: Evolve an API while preserving known client contracts and a bounded retirement path.
curriculum.production_scenario: A renamed response field breaks an older mobile client that updates slowly.
misconceptions: A version prefix does not remove the need to define compatibility.
curriculum.evidence: Run old-client fixtures against a changed schema and identify breaking cases.
curriculum.artifact: A version change proposal with compatibility tests and retirement criteria.

title: Microservices vs monolith boundaries

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose service boundaries from data ownership and operational coupling rather than team fashion.
curriculum.production_scenario: A simple purchase requires six deployments and fails when any service slows.
misconceptions: Splitting processes does not automatically produce independently changeable components.
curriculum.evidence: Map a business change to required deployments and cross-service transactions.
curriculum.artifact: A boundary decision record comparing a modular monolith and service split.

title: Service mesh and sidecar patterns

curriculum.learner_outcome: Explain which transport concerns a mesh can handle and which remain application responsibilities.
curriculum.production_scenario: Proxy retries multiply application retries during a partial regional failure.
misconceptions: A service mesh cannot infer business idempotency or fix an invalid retry policy.
curriculum.evidence: Trace attempts across proxy and application layers under one failed request.
curriculum.artifact: A transport policy with retry budgets, identity boundaries and failure tests.

title: API gateways and BFF pattern

curriculum.learner_outcome: Assign gateway responsibilities without creating opaque business logic or a single bottleneck.
curriculum.production_scenario: Several services interpret the same user identity differently behind a gateway.
misconceptions: Authenticating at the edge does not remove downstream authorization checks.
curriculum.evidence: Trace identity and failure responses across the edge and one service.
curriculum.artifact: A gateway contract with trust boundaries and capacity protection rules.

title: Real-time delivery: WebSockets, SSE, long polling

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design connection recovery and message continuity separately from the live transport.
curriculum.production_scenario: A mobile chat client reconnects after missing several server messages.
misconceptions: A persistent connection does not itself provide durable delivery or history.
curriculum.evidence: Disconnect and reconnect a client and detect missing and repeated messages.
curriculum.artifact: A real-time protocol with replay cursor and backpressure behavior.

title: Serverless architecture and cold starts

curriculum.learner_outcome: Evaluate function execution limits, retries and external state for an asynchronous workload.
curriculum.production_scenario: An image-processing function runs twice after the first attempt times out.
misconceptions: Managed execution does not eliminate duplicate work or downstream capacity limits.
curriculum.evidence: Replay duplicate invocations and calculate pressure on the storage dependency.
curriculum.artifact: A function contract with idempotency keys and concurrency budget.

title: Feature flags and progressive delivery

curriculum.learner_outcome: Use flags to control rollout while keeping compatibility and rollback behavior explicit.
curriculum.production_scenario: A disabled feature leaves data that older application code cannot read.
misconceptions: Switching off a UI flag does not undo writes made by the feature.
curriculum.evidence: Exercise enabled/disabled clients against both schema versions.
curriculum.artifact: A rollout matrix with cleanup ownership and a tested rollback boundary.

title: AuthN/AuthZ: sessions, JWT, OAuth2

curriculum.learner_outcome: Separate identity proof, session lifecycle and authorization at resource boundaries.
curriculum.production_scenario: A valid login token lets one tenant read another tenant's records.
misconceptions: Authentication success does not authorize every resource operation.
curriculum.evidence: Test expired, wrong-audience and cross-tenant requests against a policy.
curriculum.artifact: An authentication flow and an authorization test matrix.

title: Secrets management and key rotation

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design secret delivery, rotation and revocation with explicit trust and failure boundaries.
curriculum.production_scenario: A database password rotates while long-lived workers still hold the old value.
misconceptions: Encoding a secret is not encryption or access control.
curriculum.evidence: Trace rotation with overlapping versions and verify old access is removed.
curriculum.artifact: A secret inventory and a rehearsed rotation/revocation runbook.

title: DDoS protection layers

curriculum.learner_outcome: Layer admission controls to preserve service capacity under different traffic attacks.
curriculum.production_scenario: A flood of expensive anonymous queries bypasses a simple per-IP limit.
misconceptions: One rate limit cannot distinguish every legitimate burst from distributed abuse.
curriculum.evidence: Model requests, bandwidth and query cost for two attack patterns.
curriculum.artifact: A layered capacity defense with thresholds and legitimate-user tests.

title: Encryption at rest and in transit

curriculum.learner_outcome: State what transport and storage encryption protect and where plaintext remains exposed.
curriculum.production_scenario: Encrypted backups are copied to storage accessible by an overly broad service role.
misconceptions: Encryption does not compensate for granting an attacker decryption permissions.
curriculum.evidence: Trace data and key access through requests, storage and backup restore.
curriculum.artifact: A data-flow threat model and a key-access policy.

title: Observability: metrics, logs, traces

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose telemetry that can answer concrete questions about user-visible failures.
curriculum.production_scenario: Users report slow requests while host CPU dashboards remain normal.
misconceptions: Collecting more telemetry does not guarantee useful incident questions can be answered.
curriculum.evidence: Diagnose one synthetic failure using a minimal set of correlated signals.
curriculum.artifact: An instrumentation plan tied to three falsifiable failure hypotheses.

title: SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets

curriculum.learner_outcome: Define user-centered reliability indicators and evaluate an error budget over a window.
curriculum.production_scenario: An API reports high uptime while many successful responses arrive too late.
misconceptions: Host uptime is not necessarily a meaningful measure of user success.
curriculum.evidence: Compute an SLI and remaining budget from a labeled request sample.
curriculum.artifact: A service objective with exclusions, windows and alerting rationale.

title: Deployment strategies: blue-green, canary, rolling

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design a release sequence that detects harm and supports a compatible rollback.
curriculum.production_scenario: A rollback fails because the new release removed a column old code needs.
misconceptions: Replacing application binaries alone does not reverse a data migration.
curriculum.evidence: Exercise mixed-version reads and writes before promoting a canary.
curriculum.artifact: A deployment checklist with stop metrics and tested compatibility boundaries.

title: Capacity planning and autoscaling

curriculum.learner_outcome: Forecast capacity from workload shape, utilization and failure headroom assumptions.
curriculum.production_scenario: A service meets average traffic but fails when one replica is drained.
misconceptions: Average daily request volume is not enough to size peak capacity.
curriculum.evidence: Calculate headroom and validate the tightest assumption with a load sample.
curriculum.artifact: A capacity worksheet covering peak load and one failed node.

title: Distributed tracing internals

curriculum.learner_outcome: Reconstruct request causality while accounting for async work and incomplete sampling.
curriculum.production_scenario: A request queues background work whose later failure is invisible in the parent trace.
misconceptions: A missing span does not prove the corresponding operation never ran.
curriculum.evidence: Follow propagated context across a queue and identify sampling gaps.
curriculum.artifact: A traced request diagram with instrumentation and data-redaction rules.

title: Incident response and postmortems

curriculum.learner_outcome: Coordinate mitigation and communication while preserving evidence for later analysis.
curriculum.production_scenario: Several responders change production simultaneously and obscure the original failure.
misconceptions: An incident needs service restoration before a perfect root-cause explanation.
curriculum.evidence: Run a tabletop incident and document decisions with observed effects.
curriculum.artifact: A concise incident timeline, mitigation record and follow-up owners.

title: Design a URL shortener

curriculum.learner_outcome: Integrate identifier allocation, durable redirects and abuse controls into a constrained design.
curriculum.production_scenario: A popular campaign creates a hot redirect while users keep creating short links.
misconceptions: Short identifiers still need collision, expiry and ownership policies.
curriculum.evidence: Estimate load and trace create, redirect, duplicate and expired-link requests.
curriculum.artifact: A URL shortener design with a small executable lookup model.

title: Design a distributed rate limiter

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design a distributed limiter whose admission accuracy and failure policy are explicit.
curriculum.production_scenario: A multi-region API must cap expensive requests despite a regional store outage.
misconceptions: A globally exact limit may cost coordination latency or reduced availability.
curriculum.evidence: Simulate concurrent callers and quantify permitted overshoot during failure.
curriculum.artifact: A limiter prototype and an accuracy/availability tradeoff report.

title: Design a news feed (fan-out strategies)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose fan-out and retrieval strategies for unequal publishing and reading workloads.
curriculum.production_scenario: A celebrity post creates a large write burst while ordinary users need fresh feeds.
misconceptions: One fan-out strategy is not optimal for every publisher's audience size.
curriculum.evidence: Estimate work for ordinary and celebrity posts and trace delayed delivery.
curriculum.artifact: A feed architecture with backlog controls and a freshness objective.

title: Design a chat system (WhatsApp-scale)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Integrate persistent messages, live connections and reconnect behavior into a chat system.
curriculum.production_scenario: A user switches devices while one connection is offline and messages are retried.
misconceptions: Online presence does not prove a message was durably delivered or read.
curriculum.evidence: Trace one conversation through disconnects, duplicates and a server restart.
curriculum.artifact: A chat protocol and storage schema with recovery transcripts.

title: Design a notification system

curriculum.learner_outcome: Build a notification pipeline that respects preferences, quotas and duplicate effects.
curriculum.production_scenario: A provider outage creates a backlog of reminders that may become irrelevant.
misconceptions: Retrying every notification indefinitely can send stale messages and amplify outages.
curriculum.evidence: Replay a provider outage and verify expiration, preference and retry rules.
curriculum.artifact: A notification state machine and a backlog recovery simulation.

title: Design search autocomplete

curriculum.learner_outcome: Design prefix suggestions with bounded latency and a measurable freshness policy.
curriculum.production_scenario: A trending query changes quickly while millions of clients type prefixes.
misconceptions: Caching popular prefixes alone does not define ranking or update correctness.
curriculum.evidence: Measure lookup work for prefix lengths and trace a ranking update.
curriculum.artifact: A prefix-search prototype with a latency and freshness evaluation.

title: Design video streaming (YouTube-scale)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Separate ingestion, transformation and playback while budgeting bandwidth and recovery.
curriculum.production_scenario: A newly uploaded video is partially processed during a regional playback spike.
misconceptions: Uploading one large file does not produce adaptive playback variants automatically.
curriculum.evidence: Trace upload failure and playback variant selection under bandwidth changes.
curriculum.artifact: A media pipeline design with readiness states and delivery cost estimates.

title: Design ride sharing (geo-matching)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Model location freshness, candidate lookup and exclusive assignment under concurrent requests.
curriculum.production_scenario: Two nearby riders attempt to claim the same driver at once.
misconceptions: The nearest reported driver may have moved or already accepted another trip.
curriculum.evidence: Simulate competing assignments and delayed position updates.
curriculum.artifact: A dispatch state machine with invariant tests and a locality budget.

title: Design a payment system

curriculum.learner_outcome: Preserve payment invariants through retries, uncertain provider outcomes and reconciliation.
curriculum.production_scenario: A payment provider times out after charging while the order remains pending.
misconceptions: A timeout does not mean payment failed or can safely be repeated as a new intent.

title: Design a distributed key-value store

curriculum.artifact: A key-value model with failure traces and a consistency specification.

title: Design a unique ID generator (Snowflake)

curriculum.learner_outcome: Choose identifiers by evaluating uniqueness scope, ordering and clock-failure behavior.

title: Design a metrics/monitoring system

title: Event loop: macrotasks, microtasks, and rendering

curriculum.learner_outcome: Predict what a captured variable holds when a closure finally runs and choose what to capture on purpose.

title: ES modules vs CommonJS loading semantics

curriculum.production_scenario: An error thrown after an await is swallowed because a caller forgot to await the returned promise.

resolve with a thenable adds turns
curriculum.production_scenario: Two logging helpers disagree about ordering and a race in tests passes only sometimes.

title: WebAssembly linear memory, typed views, and JavaScript interop

wait and notify on shared cells

curriculum.learner_outcome: Explain which animations run on the compositor thread and why they survive main-thread jank.

curriculum.learner_outcome: Explain what the same-origin policy blocks, how CORS opts a reader in, and what CSP restricts.
